summary.headline: Rico Auto Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 852 crore but EBITDA collapsed to Rs 9.3 crore and PAT was negative Rs 26.3 crore on air-freight costs.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was Rs 852 crore with EBITDA of Rs 9.3 crore and PAT of negative Rs 26.3 crore; H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 1,607 crore, EBITDA Rs 46.9 crore and PAT negative Rs 29.7 crore. Management attributed the hit to air-freight and premium shipping costs incurred to keep single-source supplies to Toyota and BMW programs running amid Middle East disruption to shipping routes, plus cost inflation (tooling, fuel, labour) not yet passed through. Management said air shipments should end after November, customer price-recovery talks are under way (two domestic customers have agreed), and it expects a sharp Q4 recovery. Management reiterated an FY27 revenue target of more than Rs 3,200 crore. The call was dominated by shareholder frustration over repeated margin misses.

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 40 crore (as referenced in Q&A)

segments.name: Aluminium casting
segments.commentary: Contributed about 89% of Q2 revenue; focus areas are transmissions and hybrid/EV bigger components. Aluminium prices reported as softening.

segments.name: Ferrous (iron) casting
segments.commentary: Contributed about 11% of revenue; heavier components drove the new-programme execution issues. Management is discussing sourcing of low-margin light iron components out to other suppliers and seeking better prices on them.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of more than Rs 3,200 crore, driven by ramp-up of ongoing programmes and better utilisation of capacity.
Air shipments expected to stop after November 2026; shipping patterns to normalise from Q3 with a shift from air to sea freight.
Management expects a big jump in Q4 FY27 once price increases and premium-freight recovery are concluded with customers.
Expects further price increases/recoveries to close with most domestic customers by end-November/mid-December and with BMW (Germany and US) after the European holiday period.
Management expects domestic auto demand growth to continue, with a guided next-year growth of at least 10%.
capex_capacity: Capacity was expanded to machine more and ship more; the company ran parallel sea and air shipments to US and Europe.
Sea transit to the US has stretched from 5-6 weeks to 10-11 weeks, adding roughly one extra month of inventory in the pipeline.
Inventory build ahead of SOP for new Toyota and BMW programmes was disrupted by logistics delays; management said desired inventory levels are now reached.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand strong; management said Rico outgrew the industry, citing Maruti, Hero and Bajaj requirements.
Cost inflation not passed through: carbide tooling costs, fuel, energy, labour and general inflation; raw material is a pass-through but other costs were not.
Price-increase negotiations: two domestic customers have agreed, with others targeted by end-November; BMW and US customers targeted after mid-December.
One customer has already agreed to contribute to air-freight costs; discussions with other customers on recovering premium freight are ongoing.
Some low-margin light iron components are being moved to other sources or repriced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term strategy to mitigate freight and operating cost volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the roughly Rs 40 crore premium-freight cost a one-time item from logistics chaos and 50 simultaneous new-item launches. Air shipments are to end after November; price recovery from customers is being negotiated.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the quarter so weak and what is being done about management execution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it the worst quarter in recent times and apologised. It said the issues were mainly in new-product development on heavier iron components and that it is implementing lessons learned, with changes and corrections under way.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the Indian auto industry and commodity costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said aluminium prices have fallen and it hopes they stabilise at lower levels. It expects domestic demand to stay strong, with Q4 seasonally the best quarter and at least 10% growth next year.

qa_highlights.question: What opportunities exist across PV, CV, hybrid and EV segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pursuing hybrid and EV opportunities as well as ICE, citing rising hybrid trends. Aluminium focus is on transmissions and bigger hybrid/EV components.

risks_watch: Recovery of premium air-freight costs and inflation pass-through: only two domestic customers have agreed so far; BMW and US customers are not yet closed.
Whether air shipments truly end after November and whether the Q4 margin rebound materialises as guided.
Middle East disruption to shipping routes and freight rates, and any recurrence on new launches.
Profitability of iron (ferrous) components; risk of losing light, low-margin iron business.
Shareholder confidence in execution given repeated guidance misses; a small shareholder questioned management's credibility.
summary.management_tone: Apologetic and defensive on execution; management repeatedly acknowledged the quarter as the worst in recent times and admitted lessons were missed. Confidence is high on the air-freight ending and Q4 recovery, but those claims are not yet backed by closed customer agreements.
key_quotes: Mr Bhaskar this is the worst quarter we've had and let me tell you it's not been easy for us
we should be out in November the last and we won't have any airshipments after that
we should have been more agile and we could have done better
we will fall back and we'll come back to our norm and you see it in the fourth quarter a big jump

growth.why: FY27 revenue target of more than Rs 3,200 crore is reiterated, implying roughly 3,200 minus H1's 1,607 = ~1,593 crore in H2 (about double H1), but no specific capacity, order or contract numbers were given to back it; the Q4 margin jump has no figures, and price recoveries are still being negotiated.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA fell to Rs 9.3 crore on about Rs 40 crore of air-freight cost, and management guided a big Q4 jump once customer price recoveries close, but only two domestic customers have agreed so far.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue target of more than Rs 3,200 crore implies roughly Rs 1,593 crore in H2 versus Rs 1,607 crore in H1, but no order or contract figures back it and the brief calls the guidance vague.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not quantified, and the brief says capacity was already expanded with no new capex discussed, so a fresh capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only held the Rs 3,200 crore FY27 revenue target, and H1 EBITDA of Rs 46.9 crore on a single-quarter collapse gives no basis for a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 revenue of about Rs 1,593 crore must roughly double H1 while price recoveries with BMW and US customers are not closed until after mid-December and the Q4 margin rebound is unquantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is pursuing hybrid and EV bigger aluminium components and new Toyota and BMW programmes are ramping, but no specific launch dates or counts were given.

rows.label: Customer price recovery and freight pass-through
rows.why: Two domestic customers have agreed, others are targeted by end-November and BMW and US after the European holiday, and one customer already agreed to contribute to air-freight costs, against about Rs 40 crore of premium freight in Q2.

rows.label: Exit of low-margin light iron components
rows.why: Management is moving some low-margin light iron components to other sources or repricing them, which could lift ferrous margins but also risks losing that volume (ferrous is about 11% of revenue).

rows.label: Pipeline inventory normalisation after sea-freight stretch
rows.why: US sea transit has stretched from 5-6 weeks to 10-11 weeks, adding about one extra month of inventory, and management says desired inventory levels are now reached, so the build should unwind as shipping normalises.

tone.note: Management was confident that air freight ends after November and that Q4 will see a big margin jump, but it apologised for the worst quarter in recent times and admitted execution lapses on heavier iron components; shareholders pressed on repeated margin misses and credibility.
